"Neo delivered another excellent quarter, with Adjusted EBITDA of $47 million, up nearly 150% year-over-year. This reflects disciplined execution across the business, record bonded magnet volumes, continued strength in hafnium and a favourable pricing environment," said Rahim Suleman, President and Chief Executive Officer of Neo. "Based on our strong year-to-date operating performance, a healthy demand outlook, firm pricing and continued operating efficiencies, we have raised our full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $180 million to $185 million. At the midpoint, that's roughly 2.4 times our full-year 2025 Adjusted EBITDA and 26% above our prior 2026 guidance."

"We also achieved several significant strategic milestones recently that further reinforce our position as a cornerstone of Europe's rare earth supply chain, including the start of commercial production at our European magnet facility, the selection of our European Integrated Magnet Project for a grant of up to €126 million ($140 million) under the European Union Innovation Fund and the designation of Silmet 2.0 as a Strategic Project in Europe. With strong operational execution, a supportive demand environment and strategic investments underpinning our next phase of growth, Neo is well positioned to deliver long-term value."
of $47 million, Driven by Strong Pricing and Sustained Demand.

Neo's solid performance through 2026 continued in the third quarter, with Adjusted EBITDA up 145% from the third quarter of 2025. Magnequench revenue increased 42% year-over-year, driven by record volumes across several targeted growth product lines. Chemicals & Oxides delivered nearly a 70% improvement in Adjusted EBITDA year over year. Rare Metals continued its exceptional performance, as the hafnium business benefited from continued favourable pricing with stable spot volumes, and the gallium business delivered its highest-ever quarterly gross profit.
Neo Raises Full Year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA Guidance to a Range of $180 to $185 million.

Building on its strong operating performance through the first nine months of the year, sustained customer demand, firm pricing and continued operating efficiencies, Neo now expects full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $180 million to $185 million, up from its previous outlook of $140 million to $150 million. The new midpoint is roughly 2.4 times 2025 Adjusted EBITDA of $76 million and 26% above prior 2026 guidance.
European Permanent Magnet Facility Commences Commercial Production:

Neo reached a major milestone in the third quarter as its European permanent magnet facility began commercial production, shipping sintered magnets to a Tier 1 electric vehicle traction motor customer. Neo has secured multiple programs from three Tier 1 motor manufacturers, including traction motors, the most demanding magnet application, with one to two more programs expected to reach commercial production by year-end.
Neo's Integrated Magnet Project Selected for Grant of €126 million ($140 million):

Neo's vision for an integrated European magnet value chain gained strong EU support in October 2026, when Neo's European Integrated Magnet Project was selected for an EU Innovation Fund grant of up to €126 million ($140 million). The project includes separation (Silmet 2.0), metallization, Phase 1B magnet expansion and digital infrastructure. The cost of the project is expected to be approximately €400 million (US$450 million).
Neo's European Separation Facility Named a Strategic Project under the EU Critical Raw Materials Act:

Silmet 2.0, the planned modernization of Neo's separation facility in Estonia, was designated as a Strategic Project under the EU Critical Raw Materials Act. The designation is expected to bring priority access to debt financing and grant funding from the EU's new budget cycle from 2028 onwards, as well as priority administrative treatment and accelerated permitting. Silmet 2.0 is expected to triple separation capacity, add a commercial-scale heavy rare earth separation platform, and draw on new feedstock.
Neo Collaborates with Carester To Secure Heavy Rare Earth Oxides for Magnet Manufacturing:

Neo's binding term sheet with Carester, signed in August 2026, is expected to strengthen Neo's European rare earth supply chain. Carester's recycling and heavy rare earth separation facility under construction in Lacq, France, is expected to supply separated dysprosium and terbium oxides to Neo's European magnet facility. Carester is also expected to recycle swarf from Neo's magnet production and return the recovered neodymium-praseodymium ("NdPr"), dysprosium, and terbium oxides, while Silmet is expected to process Carester's mixed rare earth carbonate.
Neo Signs MOU with Rainbow Rare Earths for Offtake from the Phalaborwa Project:

As part of the September 2026 memorandum of understanding ("MOU"), Rainbow will provide Neo with offtake rights to 40% of Phalaborwa's annual production of separated NdPr oxide and 65% of the mixed heavy rare earth carbonate, containing dysprosium and terbium, from Rainbow's Phalaborwa Project in South Africa. In exchange, Neo will provide Rainbow with design input and technical support for the final solvent extraction separation circuit to achieve the Phalaborwa Project's intended mix and purity. Phalaborwa is expected to recover rare earths from stockpiled phosphogypsum, without requiring new mining. Subject to binding agreements, the arrangement is expected to provide an additional feedstock source for Silmet.

Magnequench Delivers Record Bonded Magnet Volumes and Begins Commercial Production in Europe
Adjusted EBITDA was $10.1 million in the third quarter, up 24% from the same period last year. Year-to-date Adjusted EBITDA is $29.8 million, up 33% from last year.
Record Quarter for Bonded Magnet Volumes:
Bonded magnet volumes rose 17% year-over-year, led by server cooling fan applications in AI data centers and growth in automotive applications.
Record Volumes for Heavy Rare Earth-Free Traction Motor Powders:
Bonded powders for traction motors reached record quarterly volumes as a new model year ramped.
European Permanent Magnet Facility Enters Commercial Production:
In September, the facility delivered its first commercial volumes to a Tier 1 EV traction motor customer, and one to two more programs are expected to start before year-end.
Chemicals & Oxides Delivers Strong Earnings Growth:
Adjusted EBITDA was $6.8 million in the third quarter, up almost 70% from the same period last year, reflecting solid performance in emission catalysts and favourable rare earth pricing.
Water Treatment Expands into New Markets:
The business continued to advance its new process enhancement technology, now in use with customers, and expanded into South America and Australia.
Separation Business Begins Transition to Diversified Supply:
Silmet began a planned move from legacy feed sources to a more diversified supply base, and in October Silmet 2.0 was named a Strategic Project under the EU Critical Raw Materials Act.
Rare Metals Delivers Adjusted EBITDA Improvement of Over 200 Percent:

Adjusted EBITDA was $35.2 million in the third quarter, up 206% from the same period last year, and $103.4 million year-to-date, up 235%, based on elevated pricing and sustained demand amid tight global supply.
Spot demand held firm and supply stayed tight, and customers continued to book contracts into 2027.

Gallium posted the highest gross profit in Neo's history on strong demand and elevated pricing as global supply tightened further. Rhenium had its best quarter on record on favourable pricing and superalloy demand.

Neo manufactures the building blocks of many modern technologies that enhance efficiency and sustainability. Neo's advanced industrial materials, rare earth magnetic powders and magnets, specialty chemicals, metals, and alloys are critical to the performance of many everyday products and emerging technologies across industries. Neo's products help to deliver the technologies of tomorrow to consumers today.
As at September 30, 2026, Neo had 1,624 employees and a global platform that includes manufacturing facilities located in Canada, China, Estonia, Germany, Thailand, and the United Kingdom ("
") as well as one dedicated research and development ("
") centre in Singapore. Neo has three operating segments: Magnequench, Chemicals & Oxides and Rare Metals, as well as the Corporate segment.
